intro: Step out of the light and into the rock. You are at Gümüşler Monastery, a rock settlement in Niğde province from the 8th to the 12th century AD. The frescoes in this rock-cut monastery's church are among the best preserved in Cappadocia, and they include a rare Byzantine image: the Virgin, shown smiling.
history: This rock-cut monastery was in use between the eighth and twelfth centuries, and was found by chance in 1963. In the frescoes of its main church, the Virgin is shown smiling, an extremely rare choice in Byzantine iconography. Around a courtyard lie the church, burial chambers and a wine press.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the frescoes of the main church and the smiling Virgin, then visit the burial chambers and the rock courtyard.
facts: Did you know? Because they stayed inside the rock, the frescoes were shielded from sun and damp, and their colours are brighter than in most Cappadocian churches. And look for her: in the fresco of the main church the Virgin is shown smiling, an extremely rare choice in Byzantine iconography.
outro: This brings our journey through Gümüşler Monastery to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let these colours stay bright for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
